Jasmine —

Thanks for sending. High level this looks promising; a couple of clarifying questions before we pull procurement/legal in for sign-off:

1) Tokens/sec baseline: the draft shows a pool-level commit of 12,000 tokens/sec with a per-request cap for fairness. Can you confirm how tokens/sec maps to concurrent QPS for our multimodal pipelines (images + text)? We need to model latency impact for our inference layer.

2) SLA credits: The SLO clause references a 95th percentile sustained tokens/sec target with operational credits tied to 'pool under-provisioning events'. Can you enumerate the types of events that would trigger credits and an example calculation?

3) Ramp/activation: if we sign the addendum 8/1, what is the expected timeline to have the reserved pool online and the KV cache warmed for our traffic pattern?

If you can answer these in the sync, great — otherwise a short note back will help procurement triage. I'm available Fri 07/17 at 2pm PT.

— Alex
Alex Keller | Director, AI Platforms — ClearWave Labs
akeller@clearwave.com | +1 650-555-0147

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal: capacity expansion + reserved-pool throughput addendum (ClearWave)

Jasmine / team —

Quick answers for Alex's questions so we have a crisp agenda for the sync:

1) Tokens/sec -> concurrency: For their multimodal mix we should model 1 image inference ~= 3–5x tokens cost compared to a short text completion; our recommended approach is to translate their token commit into a weighted steady-state concurrency (we'll share a small worksheet). In short: 12k tokens/sec approximates ~65–90 concurrent text-focused QPS, lower if image workloads dominate. See attached capacity-schedule-chart.xlsx for scenarios.

2) Credit triggers: We classify an under-provisioning event as when sustained observed pool throughput (five-minute window) falls below 85% of committed tokens/sec for two consecutive windows and we have no automated temporary scale or fallback available. Credits are pro-rata based on shortfall minutes multiplied by a token-rate multiplier; example calc is section 3.2 of the addendum. Operationally we'll issue a credit if the event is reproducible and not caused by customer-side, e.g., malformed requests, or force-majors.

3) Ramp: OSS provisioning time is 10 business days after contract signature; image-heavy KV-warming is typically an additional 3–5 business days of progressive traffic shaping. So signing 8/1 -> target live by ~8/17. We'll offer a one-time free warm-up window included in the first month to expedite state warm-up.

I'll bring the scenario sheet to the call and suggest we confirm the 12k baseline vs. a stepped commit (8k -> 12k over 60 days) if they prefer smoothing.

— Dylan
Dylan Brooks | Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Jasmine, go ahead and circulate a version that captures the stepped commit option and the credit example table and we'll route to DocuSign once Priya signs off.
